records.title: Practicum: Health Assessment and Foundational Skills for Nursing Practice
records.header: NCLIN 301 Practicum: Health Assessment and Foundational Skills for Nursing Practice (6)
records.text: NCLIN 301 Practicum: Health Assessment and Foundational Skills for Nursing Practice (6) Focuses on foundational nursing skills including health assessment, interviewing and communication, as well as psychomotor skills and critical thinking in the context of nursing care to individuals across the lifespan. Person-centered care and patient safety are emphasized through use of simulation.

records.title: Practicum: Health Assessment
records.text: NCLIN 302 Practicum: Health Assessment (3) First in a series of clinical courses emphasizing beginning nursing skills. These skills will include health assessment of the individual and family, communication, and interviewing. Predominant themes include communication skills, physical and psychosocial assessment of the individual across the developmental life span. Offered: A.

records.title: Practicum: Foundational Skills for Professional Nurses ([1/2]-, max. 5)
records.header: NCLIN 306 Practicum: Foundational Skills for Professional Nurses ([1/2]-, max. 5)
records.text: NCLIN 306 Practicum: Foundational Skills for Professional Nurses ([1/2]-, max. 5) Laboratory-based course focuses on psychomotor skills and critical thinking in the context of nursing care to individuals across the lifespan. Emphasizes patient safety and quality, and person-centered care through use of simulation. Prerequisite: NCLIN 302, which may be taken concurrently. Credit/no-credit only. Offered: AWSp.

records.title: Practicum: Pediatric Nursing
records.text: NCLIN 403 Practicum: Pediatric Nursing (4) Provides supervised acute/chronic illness nursing care to pediatrics clients. Emphasizes beginning skills in systematic health and developmental assessment, including person/environment fit, basic competency in selected nursing therapies, and developing role as care agent for pediatrics clients and their families. Prerequisite: NURS 401, may be taken concurrently. Credit/no-credit only. Offered: WSp.

records.title: Practicum: Nursing Care of Ill Adults
records.header: NCLIN 407 Practicum: Nursing Care of Ill Adults (5)
records.text: NCLIN 407 Practicum: Nursing Care of Ill Adults (5) Provides supervised nursing care to ill adults and their families. Emphasizes systematic assessment, including person/environment fit, developing competency in selected nursing therapies, and developing a role as a professional nurse. Prerequisite: NURS 401, which may be taken concurrently. Credit/no-credit only.

records.title: Population Health Through Community Health Nursing Partnerships
records.header: NCLIN 409 Population Health Through Community Health Nursing Partnerships (4)
records.text: NCLIN 409 Population Health Through Community Health Nursing Partnerships (4) Analysis, application, and evaluation of community partnership process for health. Analysis of nursing role in community/public health, including community building, collaboration, policy. Development and formulation of community interventions to maintain/promote biopsychosocial health, and to promote health/prevention of injury and disease. Credit/no-credit only.

records.title: Transition to Clinical Practice
records.text: NCLIN 411 Transition to Clinical Practice (7) Capstone clinical in a specialty focusing on critical examination, synthesis, and evaluation of professional nursing care. Client populations include individuals and/or groups reflecting diverse settings, ages, and ethnic communities. Emphasis on mastering theoretical concepts, applying theory and research findings, improving skill competency, and developing leadership capabilities in the clinical setting. Credit/no-credit only.

records.title: Practicum: Care of Childbearing Families
records.header: NCLIN 416 Practicum: Care of Childbearing Families (2)
records.text: NCLIN 416 Practicum: Care of Childbearing Families (2) Provides the opportunity for supervised nursing of childbearing families and individuals. Emphasizes expanding nursing process skills, especially health promotion, with individuals and families during childbearing. Prerequisite: NURS 415, which may be taken concurrently. Credit/no-credit only. Offered: WSp.

records.title: Practicum: Psychosocial Nursing
records.text: NCLIN 418 Practicum: Psychosocial Nursing (3-4) Provides supervised psychosocial nursing care to individuals/families/groups/communities with threats to or alterations in psychosocial health. Emphasizes increasing skill in systematic assessment, developing competency in selected psychosocial nursing interventions, and evaluation of treatment outcomes. Credit/no-credit only. Offered: AW.

records.title: Practicum: Ambulatory Care
records.text: NCLIN 422 Practicum: Ambulatory Care (3) Provides opportunity for simulated and supervised nursing of individuals in a variety of ambulatory care settings. Discussion of organization of ambulatory care within the health care system and role of professional nursing. Emphasizes concepts of episodic care, triage, health promotion and education, interdisciplinary communication, care coordination, and resource and environmental management. Prerequisite: NCLIN 407. Offered: A.

records.title: Foundations of Interprofessional Practice ([0-1]-, max. 3)
records.header: NCLIN 475 Foundations of Interprofessional Practice ([0-1]-, max. 3)
records.text: NCLIN 475 Foundations of Interprofessional Practice ([0-1]-, max. 3) Team-based training in healthcare team functioning for professional nursing students. Students work and co-learn with other health sciences students in applying knowledge of evidence-based practice, quality improvement principles, and informatics to patient-centered care situations. The course will provide careful attention to development of intra- and interprofessional roles and professional identity. Credit/no-credit only. Offered: AWSp.

records.title: Clinical Practicum Elective
records.text: NCLIN 499 Clinical Practicum Elective (1-5) Provides opportunities to develop nursing skills in the care of individuals, groups, communities, or care-systems. Individually arranged with faculty member for application of theory and principles to direct care, consultation, education, or care coordinator roles. Prerequisite: NCLIN 302; NCLIN 306; NCLIN 402; NCLIN 406.
